clue.text: Rock group with means to go glam and bring harmony back

parts.note: Kiss are the American rock band famous for face paint
and means together with
make-up is what one uses to look glamorous

explanation.surface: A face-painted rock band uses cosmetics to glam up and patch up their quarrels.
explanation.definitionFit: To make friends again after a quarrel is to restore harmony, the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Chaste woman and partner beset by primitive urges, overwhelmed!

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the urges wrap round the woman and her partner

parts.note: the id is Freud's seat of primitive instinctive urges
a nun is a woman vowed to chastity
a date is a romantic partner

explanation.surface: A celibate woman and her companion are swamped by base desires.
explanation.definitionFit: Flooded and swamped are synonyms, so being swamped by work or water fits.

clue.text: Bubbly? Yes, I'd guess regularly knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back, like a drink swallowed, means the picked letters are read backwards
regularly means taking every other letter of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Asked whether something is fizzy, a drinker guesses yes after downing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the odd letters YSDUS from 'Yes, I'd guess' and 'knocked back' turns them round. The question mark marks a looser definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foamy with soapy lather is bubbly, a near synonym.

clue.text: Egyptian ruler wanting month off

parts.note: wanting means lacking, giving no as in 'no money'
March is the third month of the year

explanation.surface: A pharaoh-era official longs for a month's holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' just joins the surface: read 'wanting month' as 'no March'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomarch governed a nome, a province of ancient Egypt, so was a regional ruler there.

clue.text: Coach and horse engaged in paper round

indicators.note: engaged in means held inside, so the horse sits within the paper
round means turned about, so the paper word is read backwards

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A trainer and his horse are absorbed in a newspaper delivery round.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports team's coach is its manager, especially in football.

clue.text: Jokes about government with zero diplomacy

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jokes word encloses the rest

parts.note: kids is a verb meaning jokes or teases
love is zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Teasing politicians while achieving nothing is hardly tactful statecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating someone with kid gloves is handling them gently and tactfully, an idiom for tact.

clue.text: Shadowy Parisian hotel room may contain it

parts.note: un is the French word for a, as a Parisian would say
lit is French for bed, the thing a hotel room contains

explanation.surface: A dim French hotel room might hold some unseen object.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay in French: 'un lit' is 'a bed', which a hotel room in Paris may well contain.
explanation.definitionFit: A place without lights burning is dark and shadowy.

clue.text: Sellers in the cinema forced to stock rum by the litre

indicators.note: to stock means to hold within, so the forced word encloses the rest

parts.note: drove means forced, as in drove them out
rum is old British slang for strange
L is the abbreviation for litre

explanation.surface: Salesmen at the picture house are made to keep rum in by the litre.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Sellers played the title role in Kubrick's 1964 film, so the definition is Sellers on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: The scientist in the 1964 Kubrick satire is one of Peter Sellers's most famous film roles.

clue.text: Tabloid reporter's correcting backward sort of communication

parts.note: the Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: reporter's suggests a word spoken, so the correcting word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: righting means correcting

explanation.surface: A tabloid journalist fixes a garbled reversed message.
explanation.definitionFit: Script written in reverse so it reads normally in a looking-glass is a backward way of conveying words.

clue.text: One providing deliveries, who tends to pitch striking opener

indicators.note: striking means removing, and opener is the first letter, so the initial goes

parts.note: a groundsman tends the pitch at a cricket ground

explanation.surface: A cricket groundsman who knocks down an opening batsman is credited with deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliveries' and 'opener' tempt a cricket reading of bowling; the definition means a tradesman delivering goods door to door.
explanation.definitionFit: A milkman or other tradesman on a delivery route is a roundsman.

clue.text: Food store investing hard capital

indicators.note: investing means clothing or surrounding, so the food store wraps round

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A grocery shop puts hard cash into business.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian capital, New Delhi, lies within the city of Delhi.

clue.text: Trifle contains divine alcoholic drink

indicators.note: contains means the trifle word holds the divine one inside

parts.note: to toy with something is to trifle with it
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a divine

explanation.surface: A sherry trifle holds a heavenly boozy dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot mix of whisky, water, sugar and spice is a classic alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Governor to go off with a pistol to the east

indicators.note: to the east means the pieces are written heading back from the east end, read backwards

parts.note: to rot is to go off, like food
a Luger is a German pistol

explanation.surface: A state governor is about to run off armed with a handgun towards the east.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor on an engine is a device that regulates speed.

clue.text: Early Christian city not for nothing needing church

parts.note: anti means against, not for
O is the round zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An early Christian town against nothing still needs a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch in Syria was where followers of Jesus were first called Christians.

clue.text: Mobile not working by south coast resort, ringing compiler up

indicators.note: working means operating on, so the letters of not are rearranged
ringing means encircling, so the resort goes round the compiler

parts.note: Hove is a resort beside Brighton on England's south coast

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the compiler refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A mobile phone is dead at a seaside town, so the setter phones in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile' looks like a phone; it is the adjective meaning moving about.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mobile is travelling or moving about.

clue.text: One bolts from Amazon, perhaps admitting tax evasion, initially

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the river holds the initials

parts.note: the Amazon is an example of a river

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of tax and evasion

explanation.surface: Someone flees the Amazon jungle after confessing to dodging tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One bolts' reads as someone fleeing; here it is a worker who fixes things with rivets.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who fastens metal plates with rivets is fastening them like bolts.

clue.text: Learner stops getting fond of lecture

indicators.note: stops means plugs, so the learner fills a gap in the phrase

parts.note: taking to someone is getting fond of them
L is the learner sign on British cars

explanation.surface: A student stops liking a dull lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: A scolding or telling-off is a stern lecture.

clue.text: Leave one's spouse? Then settle equitably

parts.note: go means leave
Dutch, as in 'my old Dutch', is Cockney rhyming slang for wife

explanation.surface: Someone walks out on a husband or wife, then divides the property fairly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my old Dutch' (from Duchess of Fife) is Cockney slang for one's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Splitting a bill evenly is sharing costs fairly.

clue.text: Punk playing loud interrupts household no end

indicators.note: interrupts means breaks into, so the rearranged letters go inside
no end means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: home means household

indicators.note: playing means performing, so the letters of loud are rearranged

explanation.surface: A punk band's loud music disrupts a family no end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punk' suggests the music, echoed by 'playing loud'; here it means a young thug.
explanation.definitionFit: Punk in older American usage is a young thug or gangster.

clue.text: Horrid urinals surrounded by water

indicators.note: horrid suggests a mess, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Disgusting public toilets are flooded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounded by water' looks like flooded toilets; it is the island sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Insular literally means like an island, cut off by sea on all sides.

clue.text: One old play about start of nouvelle vague

indicators.note: about means going round, so the pieces surround the initial letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
ex means former, old
an act is part of a play, or to play a role

indicators.note: start of takes the first letter of nouvelle

explanation.surface: A single dated play centres on the beginning of French New Wave cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nouvelle vague' is the French New Wave of film; 'vague' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imprecise or not exact is vague.

clue.text: Nimble light infantry, miles away from the battle

parts.note: LI is the abbreviation for light infantry

indicators.note: away from means taken out of, so the miles letter is removed

parts.note: the Somme was a First World War battle

explanation.surface: Agile soldiers are far from the battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe and supple, light on one's feet, means agile.

clue.text: Topless celebrity with silicone body parts

indicators.note: topless in a down clue means the top letter is removed

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
Si is the chemical symbol for silicon, of which silicone is a compound

explanation.surface: A bare-chested celeb with silicone implants shows off parts of her body.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarsal bones form the ankle and foot, parts of the body.

clue.text: Cape and grass skirts modish

indicators.note: skirts means goes round the edge, so the grass word encloses the other

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis, grass
in means fashionable, modish

explanation.surface: A cloak and a grass skirt are fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland jutting into the sea is called a point or a cape.

clue.text: With media manipulation, rogue gets to improve appearance

parts.note: PR is public relations, managing the media
an imp is a little rogue

explanation.surface: A rascal with good spin doctors manages to look better.
explanation.definitionFit: To primp is to groom oneself fussily, making one's looks better.

clue.text: Back very sore, needing massage

indicators.note: a massage works and kneads, so the letters of sore are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone with a very painful back wants a massage.
explanation.definitionFit: The reverse of a page, the left-hand side, is called its back.

clue.text: Tempting sort of meat dog's eaten

indicators.note: eaten here means taken in, so the meat surrounds the dog

parts.note: lean meat has little fat
a dingo is an Australian wild dog

explanation.surface: A dog has gobbled a piece of tempting meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'dog's' means 'has': the dog has been eaten by the meat word.
explanation.definitionFit: Leading someone on is enticing or misleading them with false hopes.

clue.text: Homer apt to display this linguistic solecism?

parts.note: the letters of homer apt are a jumbled version of a figure of speech, so they display that figure mixed

explanation.surface: Would the poet Homer be liable to produce this muddled figure of speech?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: rearrange METAPHOR and you get 'Homer apt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Combining two incompatible images, like 'nip it in the bud before it snowballs', is a linguistic blunder.
